medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
Our students get involved with organizations such as LMSA & SNMA to provide mentorship & programming to address the needs of the community & issues related to minority health. Students from LMSA/SNMA are actively involved in the admissions process and have a student representative on the Admissions Committee.  Our student groups are open to all students!

The Office of Student Engagement & Community offers academic and personal support for ALL medical students, assists with recruitment, and works to ensure that every student feels a true sense of belonging in our school community.

We also have a First Gen student group that supports students who are first generation high school, college, or first in their family to pursue medicine.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Requests for a leave of absence must be approved by the Associate Deans for Student Affairs. A leave of absence must be completed in one year and if necessary, a second year may then be requested.  The MD degree must be awarded within six (6) calendar years of initial matriculation, except for those students in the Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP).
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Our students participate in nearly forty student organizations. We support & encourage the creativity & energy of our students, whose initiative & leadership have led to the creation of many of these groups. Student organizations at the School of Medicine are much more than a conduit for exploring medical interests with peers; they also provide valuable opportunities to develop leadership skills & extraordinary opportunities to work with faculty, members of the community, national medical practitioners, & researchers.  

Growth outside of the classroom is important, and many students get involved in such activities as intramural sports, dance, rock climbing, running, yoga, biking, martial arts, among other activities, and also engage with the local, vibrant music and food scenes.

Additionally, nearly all of our students participate in some way in the annual Doc Opera performance.  Doc Opera has been an annual tradition for 41 years & is completely student-run. https://bit.ly/2R3SKDE
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The University is located approximately 3 miles from downtown Cleveland. The School of Medicine is located near the University's 150-acre campus in the city's University Circle area, a cultural and educational hub for the City of Cleveland.  The Health Education Campus is adjacent to the Cleveland Clinic, and our other teaching hospitals are nearby. The Northeast Ohio region is positioning itself to become a global center of excellence in healthcare.

University Circle:  http://www.universitycircle.org 
Visitors Bureau: http://www.thisiscleveland.com/

CWRU and Cleveland Clinic partnered to build the state-of-the-art Health Education Campus which not only houses the medical school MD programs but also includes the School of Nursing, School of Dental Medicine, and the Physician Assistant program. The 477,000 square foot structure was completed in spring, 2019.
Read more: http://hec.case.edu
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Graduate, on-campus housing is not available but ample housing exists within walking distance in the surrounding neighborhoods. One of the benefits of attending CWRU is the affordability and availability of local, reasonably priced housing.  Rents average $1,100 month.  

Students live in a variety of settings including apartments, two-family houses, rooms in private homes, and single-family houses that several students rent together.  Many students utilize the University's shuttle service or the public transit system to get to school.  Student parking is also nearby.

Medical Student Life in Cleveland: https://youtu.be/urnL9_kI8ec
Living and Learning in University Circle: https://youtu.be/Ow3-RHCmmis
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:

medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The School of Medicine supports applicants and students with disabilities by facilitating access to reasonable accommodations through the central Disability Resources office. Beyond formal accommodations, students are supported by their Academic Societies, where Society Deans provide personal and academic advising, including referrals for accommodated testing and learning assistance. All students are required to attest annually to their ability to meet the medical school’s Technical Standards, ensuring they can successfully fulfill the essential functions of the curriculum.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Our medical school is deeply committed to fostering wellness among our students, recognizing that the journey through medical education is as much about personal growth as it is about academic achievement. We understand that the well-being of our future healthcare professionals is paramount, not only for their success but also for the quality of care they will provide to their patients. Therefore, our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to integrate opportunities for self-care and wellness. This is achieved through a balanced schedule that allows for adequate rest, physical activities, and personal time. We also offer resources and programs focused on mental health, stress management, and resilience-building through our Office of Student Affairs. By ensuring our students have the time and support to engage in self-care activities, we are nurturing a generation of physicians who value their well-being as much as their professional responsibilities. 

At our medical school, we recognize the diverse needs of our student body, which is why we are proud to have dedicated spaces such as the Prayer and Reflection Room and the Wellness Room within our building. The Prayer and Reflection Room provides a tranquil and respectful environment where students of all faiths and beliefs can engage in private prayer, meditation, or quiet contemplation. Similarly, the Wellness Room is a serene space designed to promote mental and physical relaxation, offering a peaceful retreat from the rigors of medical studies. These rooms are a testament to our commitment to supporting the holistic well-being of our students, acknowledging the importance of spiritual, emotional, and mental health in the demanding journey of medical education.

Finally, The Mandel Wellness and Preventive Care Pathway equips students for excellence in holistic wellness, providing the tools to promote healthy lifestyles in themselves and their future patients. https://case.edu/medicine/wellness-pathway/about
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our medical school culture is a vibrant mix of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, with students from 30–40 states and several countries coming together to create a dynamic and welcoming community. Diversity isn’t just a statistic here—it shapes how we learn, connect, and grow together.

While medical school is challenging, that doesn’t mean it isn’t fun. Collaboration is at the heart of our classrooms, where rigorous academics meet lively discussions, creative problem-solving, and plenty of camaraderie. Whether it’s late-night study sessions that turn into inside jokes, student-led events, or impromptu coffee breaks, our students find ways to support each other while making lasting memories.

We believe balance is key. Students are encouraged to step away from the books, pursue hobbies, get involved in the community, and spend time with friends and family. A well-rounded life not only keeps you sane - it makes you a better physician.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo:
The unique opportunity for students to participate in experiences at multiple varied affiliate hospital city-wide necessitates that students have available transportation for all four years. Required pre-clinical experiences begin as early as the first months of medical school.

It is expected that you will have access to reliable transportation for purposes of attending scheduled clinical activities.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
University Program (4 yr. MD): If you like to talk, teach, and collaborate, our Case Inquiry (IQ) curriculum at Western Reserve2 revolutionizes learning. Adapted from McMaster University's Problem-Based Learning, small groups of 8-9 students and a faculty facilitator tackle cases three times a week. Students set weekly learning goals, then research and discuss on Wednesdays and Fridays to collaboratively build knowledge and understand key concepts. This immersive, student-centered journey emphasizes deep learning, teamwork, professionalism, and critical thinking, while also enhancing clinical reasoning, patient presentation, and interprofessional education.

Lerner College Program (5 yr. MD): The LCP (LCP) offers a 5-year innovative medical school program with a mission to train physician investigators and includes a required research thesis year with formal defense and full tuition scholarship for each student. The curriculum emphasizes problem-based learning with no formal lectures, grades, or class rankings, fostering a collaborative rather than competitive environment. Students benefit from a high faculty-to-student ratio with mentors drawn from 3,000+ Cleveland Clinic experts, graduating with a Special Qualification in Biomedical Research.

Phone: 1.866.735.1912
Email: cclcm@ccf.org
IG: @clecliniclcm
https://my.clevelandclinic.org/lerner-college-medicine 

Due to character limits, we recommend that you visit our website where you will find more detailed descriptions of our three MD tracks: https://case.edu/medicine/education/medical-education/md-programs

The Pathways Programs at our school are parallel programs designed to provide individualized enrichment experiences for University Program students with interest or expertise in pursuits beyond the core curriculum. Each Pathway has a unique curriculum and think of a pathway like getting a "minor" during medical school. More about the Pathways: https://case.edu/medicine/md/academics/pathways-programs

medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our Mission
To improve health globally by linking groundbreaking innovation and research directly to patients and populations, within a world class ecosystem of medicine and education.

Our Approach
We utilize an extraordinary consortium of medical school faculty across all Cleveland medical institutions to create integrated teams of experts to educate our trainees, link disciplines to discover the mysteries and treatment of serious diseases, and understand and eliminate health inequities in Cleveland and across the world. Our mission guides us to provide excellence in medical education through our unique curriculum, advance discoveries from our laboratories to patients and improve the health of our community.

Since 1843, the CWRU School of Medicine has been dedicated to enhancing human health and has been a leader and innovator in the fields of medical education and biomedical research. Building upon its proud history while embracing today's challenges, the School's mission remains unchanged: to educate future physicians who will care for patients with mastery, creativity, and compassion, in a setting that fosters collegiality, leadership, and excellence in scholarship and research.

The goal of our admissions process is to further the mission of the Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine, which includes excellence in medical education, discoveries in translational science, and improving community health. To best meet the needs of the patient populations in Ohio and beyond and to achieve the goals of the institution, the School of Medicine's admissions process uses a balanced approach that considers an applicant's academic metrics, experiences, and personal attributes in order to achieve the educational benefits of a student body and future physician work force.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
The Pre-Professional Scholars Program (PPSP) offers undergraduate admission and conditional admission to Case Western Reserve University’s School of Medicine MD Program.

Admission to PPSP is highly competitive for high school seniors applying to college. Applicants who are not selected for the program may still be considered for undergraduate admission to Case Western Reserve University; many choose to enroll in the first-year class. Application to the program is initiated during the college application process.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
- 3-5 Letters of Recommendations. At least two should be from science advisors/professors; or
- 1 Pre-Medical Committee evaluation letter will be accepted in lieu of the 3-5 individual letters. Some committee letters consist of a single letter, with no additional letters attached, while others include the committee letter as well as letters from other recommenders. If your committee provides the former, with no additional letters attached, then you will need to submit an additional two letters of recommendation, with at least one from a research advisor, science advisor, or science course instructor. The other letter can be from a recommender of your choice. Please check with your premedical committee if you are unsure which format they provide.
- 1 letter from a research mentor is required for the College Program and MSTP.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Interview days include interviews and interactions with faculty members and medical students.  They also include information sessions, a virtual tour, and interactive activities.  Interview days at our school are full day events that also allow interviewees to get to know us and to get a feel for our student body, community, and educational environment.  All of our interviewers have participated in implicit bias training. Opportunities to attend periodic online "meet & greets" with our student groups (SNMA/LMSA, LGBTQ+, First Gen, and Parents & Partners) are available to all interviewees.  Additionally, our medical students host "You Do IQ" sessions to give interviewees an opportunity to get a taste of how small group learning works in the University Program.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Although strong academic credentials are important in the admissions process, equally important are interpersonal skills, exposure to medicine, well-roundedness, and qualities such as professionalism, empathy, and leadership ability.

Applicants for admission must complete a course of study leading to a baccalaureate degree at an accredited U.S. or Canadian college or university prior to matriculation. If you have received your undergraduate degree outside the U.S. or Canada, you must complete at least one year of advanced science-based coursework at an accredited U.S. institution prior to application. This can be achieved through a master’s or Ph.D. degree, a formalized post-baccalaureate program, or through a variety of upper-level science coursework.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our Admissions Committee sees all scores from MCAT attempts and considers the most recent MCAT score in the decision making process.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
To receive a secondary application, an applicant must have a minimum MCAT score of at least 495. 

If you submit your AMCAS application before a pending MCAT score has been reported, you must indicate any future dates when you intend to take the MCAT. We will not send you an invitation to our secondary application until the MCAT score is received and it meets our minimum threshold score of 495. Please do not submit your application until you have decided whether you will retake the MCAT.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Not applicable - we don't have a minimum undergraduate GPA. Applicants must meet the pre-requisite coursework requirements prior to matriculation.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo:
Not applicable  - as each applicant is evaluated holistically within the context of their application.

The ranges of the academic metrics for those that were invited to interview were:

Cumulative Undergraduate GPA: 2.56-4.00
MCAT: 503-528

The average GPA and MCAT for the entering class of 2025 was: 

3.91 Cumulative Undergraduate GPA with a range of 3.12-4.00
3.87 Undergraduate Science GPA with a range of 3.03-4.00
517 MCAT with a range of 505-526, Mode: 518
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo:
Not applicable - we don't have a minimum number of credit hours that need earned in post bacc. Applicants must meet the pre-requisite requirements. Science credit hours typically seen with our successful applications at the time of application are:

 - Non-science majors: at least 40 credit hours
 - Science majors: at least 55 credit hours
 - Post-bacc students: at least 32 credit hours

Note that these are simply guidelines to help you as you structure your course of study and that there can be exceptions.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: If ALL science pre-requisites were taken at a community college, we strongly recommend that you take at least a year of upper-level sciences from an accredited four-year degree granting university within the United States or Canada. If a few science pre-requisites were taken at a community college, we will evaluate them on a case-by-case basis.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo:
University Program (4-Year MD) & Lerner College Program (5-Year MD):
Updates are only accepted from applicants who have been invited for an interview. Given the extensive scope and detailed content of the application, we have sufficient information within it to make a decision regarding the interview. Both programs accept Letters of Intent and Letters of Interest after the interview, as well as updates from applicants who are placed on the waitlist following the interview. These letters provide valuable insight into an applicant’s commitment to the program and alignment with its mission.

MSTP (Medical Scientist Training Program):
Accepts research-related updates from applicants prior to the interview. Letters of Intent and Letters of Interest are accepted after the interview and from applicants who are placed on the waitlist following the interview. These letters are important for conveying the applicant’s continued interest in the program and demonstrating a strong fit with the MSTP’s goals. The MSTP also accepts application updates, Letters of Intent, and Letters of Interest from applicants on the waitlist after the interview..
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: All matriculating students must review and meet the school's Technical Standards, which outline the essential physical, cognitive, and behavioral abilities required to complete the medical curriculum.  Additionally, medical students have to review and sign an attestation every year regarding their ability to meet the technical standards. This policy also details the process for students to formally request reasonable accommodations through the University's Office of Disability Resources, should they be needed.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Financial aid for the University Program is based on demonstrated financial need. Merit scholarships are not issued.  Financial aid applications for University Program students become available in January, with awards made in April. College Program & MSTP students do not pay tuition or continuation fees.

The CWRU SOM Office of Financial Aid has developed a financial wellness & debt management curriculum called "Money Matters" that is longitudinal across all four years of medical school.  It is designed to offer our students resources and sessions to help build skills surrounding financial literacy that will last beyond the time spent in medical school. This program also includes one-on-one budgeting and financial check-ins with a student's Money Mentor.

Please note that the University Program is unable to provide financial aid assistance to non-US citizens or individuals with DACA status.  International and DACA students who are accepted to the College Program are eligible for their full-tuition scholarship.

SOM Office of Financial Aid: https://case.edu/medicine/students/financial-aid

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The School of Medicine seeks to cultivate a diverse student body and values both visible and invisible forms of diversity. Students are selected without regard to age, nationality, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or state of residence.

All candidates must demonstrate exceptional academic strength and meaningful personal achievements and are evaluated through a holistic review process. Every component of the application, including essays and letters of recommendation, is carefully considered.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
While shadowing can be extremely valuable, other clinically and medically related experiences are equally important components of career exploration. Our Admissions Committee strongly recommends medically related experiences, as they are pivotal to understanding the nuances of the medical profession.

Engaging in these opportunities allows aspiring physicians to gain firsthand insight into the realities of medical practice - from patient care to the complexities of healthcare systems. Such exposure is essential for confirming one’s passion for and commitment to the field. Furthermore, developing a clear and realistic understanding of what a career in medicine entails is critical to making an informed decision about pursuing this challenging yet rewarding path.

These experiences not only deepen an applicant’s understanding but also demonstrate dedication and preparedness for the rigorous journey toward becoming a physician.
